English: Royal Donjon
The fortress is crowned with a mighty stone donjon, symbol of royal power, with broad quarters, high towers, and command of the realm.
Bailey Citadel
A grand inner bailey is constructed, with thickest walls and elite garrison quarters, offering unmatched last-resort defense.
Command Post
A fortress-within-a-fortress, with war rooms, signal towers, and master-at-arms, serving as the nerve center of the entire garrison.
Marksman's Bastion
The pinnacle of medieval archery defense: vast stone bastions with internal galleries, murder holes, advanced firing angles, and space for elite marksmen to dominate the battlefield.
Master Engineer's Forge
A legendary forge and command center where only the most skilled engineers craft and innovate the most formidable siege engines, unrivaled in both defense and attack.
Veterans' Quarters
Luxurious apartments and strategic rooms for veteran warriors, commanders, and their retainers, granting superior command and fortitude.
Fortress Keep
The entire complex is upgraded to a true fortress: multi-layered walls, bastions, and a central citadel command hall.
Grand Gatehouse

The ultimate in medieval gate fortification: a towering, multi-tiered stone gatehouse complex with advanced defensive mechanisms, murder holes, multiple drawbridges, and living quarters for elite guards.
Crossfire Platform
Large, interconnected wall platforms allowing multiple units of archers to coordinate deadly crossfire on all approaches, maximizing the defensive reach of the fort.
Advanced Siege Works
A sprawling, fortified complex dedicated to the mass production, repair, and innovation of siege machinery. Greatly increases the fort's ability to withstand and inflict sieges.
Armored Garrison
A heavily reinforced barracks with stone vaults and armories, housing elite soldiers and advanced siege defenses.
Round Keep
The main keep is rebuilt in a round design, eliminating blind spots and improving resistance to undermining and siege engines.
Fortified Entrance
A massive, stone-reinforced entrance with reinforced towers, improved parapets, and layered portcullises, creating a nearly impenetrable gateway.
Shooting Turret
Specialized round or polygonal turrets projecting from the wall, supporting enfilade fire and offering archers protected vantage points at corners and gates.
Siege Engine Hall
A grand hall of stone where master engineers oversee the production and deployment of a variety of siege engines, greatly empowering both defense and offense.
Drill Yard
A fortified training ground within the barracks complex, where soldiers hone their skills under the watch of experienced officers.
Barbican Entry
A strong outer barbican with towers, walls, and secondary gates, providing another obstacle before reaching the main gate.
Sentinel Keep

A fortress-scale watchtower complex with curtain walls, drawbridge, and integrated barracks. Garrisoned by elite archers and officers, it forms the ultimate bulwark and command hub against any threat.
Square Keep
A massive square stone keep rises at the center, housing nobles and officers, and providing command over the entire fortress.
Covered Gallery
Fully enclosed wooden and stone passageways atop the walls, sheltering archers from incoming missiles while allowing concentrated volleys in defense.
Observation Tower
A masterwork tower with high vantage points, telescopic sighting devices, and permanent staff of scouts and cartographers, ensuring unmatched intelligence gathering and defense coordination.
Trebuchet Workshop
A stone and timber hall where the most advanced siege engines, such as trebuchets, are constructed and tested. Represents a leap in siege warfare.
Double Gatehouse
A pair of gatehouses with a killing ground between them, forcing attackers to breach two separate sets of gates under concentrated missile fire.
Troop Dormitory
A multi-story stone building with dedicated training yards and improved facilities, housing a large force and enabling swift reinforcement.
Beacon Tower
The realms primary signal point, this tall stone tower is crowned with massive beacon fires visible for leagues. Extra garrison and messengers guarantee the alarm spreads instantly.
Moated Keep
A deep moat is dug around the walls, with drawbridges and reinforced towers, deterring all but the most determined attackers.
Fortress Warehouse
A sprawling stone warehouse integrated into the fort's walls, with vast storage, secure vaults, and storehouses for both supplies and equipment.
Drawbridge Gate
The entrance is fortified with a counterweighted drawbridge spanning a ditch or moat, greatly increasing the fortress' ability to repel direct assault.
Defended Parapet
A reinforced, elevated parapet lined with murder holes and arrow loops, allowing for relentless defensive fire and greater protection for elite archers.
Catapult Yard
A walled yard dedicated to the construction and maintenance of catapults. Greatly enhances siege attack and defensive strength.
High Watchtower
A towering stone structure rising above the landscape, with reinforced battlements, advanced signaling, and ballista emplacements. Houses elite sentries and provides unrivaled visibility.
Barracks Hall
A spacious stone barracks, complete with armory, sleeping quarters, and a mess hall for the garrison.
Ceremonial Courtyard
A magnificent stone-paved court adorned with banners and statues, used for rallies, knightings, and the spectacle of lordly rule.
Stockade Redoubt
A formidable redoubt, its thick timbered walls layered with stone and earth, designed for last stands. Bristling with arrow slits and reinforced gates, it dominates the landscape.
Gatehouse Keep
A fortified gatehouse with murder holes, portcullis, and barracks is built into the curtain wall, vastly improving entry defense.
Murder Hole Gatehouse
A stone gatehouse equipped with murder holes and arrow slits, allowing defenders to pour missiles and boiling oil upon attackers beneath the gate arch.
Quartermaster Depot
A large, organized depot with dedicated staff, detailed ledgers, and disciplined rationing, maximizing readiness and minimizing waste.
Ballista Shed
A reinforced shed for the assembly and storage of ballistae, enabling defenders to deploy powerful bolt-throwers during sieges.
Enclosed Watchtower
A stone watchtower surrounded by a defensive wall and moat, with improved living quarters and stores, ensuring the garrison can hold out during extended sieges.
Machicolation Wall
Stone galleries with floor openings (machicolations) overhanging the walls, enabling defenders to rain arrows and missiles directly onto besiegers below.
Cold Storage
A stone-built, well-ventilated cold storage house with clever insulation, safeguarding vast reserves for years and ensuring the fort's survival in siege or famine.
Great Hall Court
A grand courtyard adjoining the lord's hall, where retinues gather and feasts are held. The very heart of the stronghold's power.
Timber Curtain
A continuous timber wall with integrated towers and fighting platforms, rivalling early stone fortifications in defensive power.
Drawbridge Moat
A formidable moat equipped with a sturdy drawbridge, allowing defenders to control access while maximizing protection.
Garrison Lodge
A fortified timber lodge with stone foundations, serving as a central barracks for trained soldiers and a stockade for defense.
Curtain Wall
Thick stone curtain walls are added, linking towers and enclosing the keep with a defensive perimeter and small gate.
Portcullis Gate
A heavy wooden portcullis, iron-reinforced, installed to stop attackers and withstand battering, with improved defensive platforms and loopholes.
Siege Supplies
A stone and timber magazine storing siege rations, pitch, and repair materials, essential for enduring long blockades or assaults.
Earthwork Rampart
A massive defensive bank of packed earth, fronted by ditches and topped with a wooden wall, offering strong resistance to scaling or ramming.
Assembly Plaza
A broad, stone-paved space for mustering levies, making proclamations, and holding public ceremonies. Authority is displayed here.
Weapon Workshop
A timber-framed structure with forges and anvils, producing weapons, shields, and basic siege implements. Attracts skilled craftsmen and allows the outfitting of more defenders.
Stone Battlement
A permanent stone parapet with crenellations, offering superior cover and firing positions for archers and defenders atop the walls.
Smokehouse
A sturdy wooden smokehouse for curing meats and fish, greatly extending their shelf life and securing long-term provisions.
Stone Watchtower
A solid stone tower with arrow slits, offering far greater durability and protection. Features a permanent guardroom and a small storeroom.
Fortified Palisade
Massive wooden works with earth embankments, stone-reinforced gates, and fire-hardened walls. A true stronghold, formidable even to seasoned attackers.
Stone-Lined Moat
A moat reinforced with cut stone, highly resistant to sapping and collapse.
Paved Courtyard
The central ground is laid with stone, allowing troops and supplies to move swiftly and giving the fort an air of permanence.
Guardhouse
A sturdy timber guardhouse with watch posts, providing improved security, discipline, and organization for the garrison.
Inner Moat
A secondary moat within the fortification, creating another barrier for attackers who breach the outer defenses.
Stone Tower
A sturdy stone-built tower replaces wood, providing a real refuge and vantage. Rudimentary kitchens and storerooms appear within.
Water-Filled Moat
A deep moat filled with water, greatly hindering siege equipment and dissuading attackers.
Patrol Tower
A tall stone tower with attached stables and barracks, supporting mounted patrols and rapid response to threats. Enhanced observation posts for round-the-clock vigilance.
Guarded Gatehouse
A timber gatehouse with watch platforms and a small guardroom, allowing defenders to keep vigilant watch over entry.
Defensive Moat
A wide, dry defensive moat carved around the fort, making direct assault difficult.
Armory Store
A secure wooden armory for storing weapons and armor, enabling quick arming of militia in times of need.
Double Palisade
Two layers of strong wooden walls, with a killing ground between. Attackers must breach two barriers under fire from defenders.
Flooded Ditch
A wide, water-filled ditch drawn from nearby rivers or wells, impeding infantry and cavalry assaults.
Engineer's Hut
A wooden hut for skilled engineers to draft plans and coordinate construction. Enables the building of simple engines and provides a modest boost to siege capabilities.
Wooden Hoarding
Temporary wooden structures projecting from the top of the wall, shielding defenders and allowing them to fire directly down on attackers.
Root Cellar
A partially sunken stone-lined cellar, cool and insulated, to preserve root vegetables and perishable supplies through harsh seasons.
Wooden Watchtower
A tall timber tower with a sheltered platform, providing improved sightlines and a protected place for lookouts. Guards quarters and basic armory included.
Lined Moat
A moat reinforced with timber or stone lining to prevent collapse and increase durability.
Signal Tower
A fortified stone tower equipped with brazier platforms and signaling horns to relay warnings swiftly across the realm. Garrison rotates to maintain constant vigilance.
Garden Court
A small plot is cultivated in the courtyard, providing fresh produce and a measure of tranquility amid the hardships of frontier life.
Watchtower Palisade
Timber towers rise above the walls, granting defenders superior sightlines. Communication and coordination greatly improve.
Guarded Palisade
A manned wooden wall with simple walkways. Sentries and lookout posts allow for early warning and swift response to threats.
Barracks Shed
An expanded log structure with makeshift bunks, offering better shelter and storage for weapons and supplies.
Provision Depot
A fortified supply yard with guarded sheds and ration stores, ensuring reliable distribution of food and water for the fort's defenders.
Earthen Trench
A deeper and more structured earthwork, offering improved defense and providing cover for defenders.
Reinforced Gate
The gate is strengthened with additional timber and rudimentary iron fittings, offering improved resistance to attacks.
Workshop Tent
A sturdy canvas tent where basic siege components and tools are assembled. Offers primitive shelter to craftsmen and helps organize the labor force.
Motte Tower
A rough timber watchtower atop an earthen motte, surrounded by makeshift fortifications, tents, and simple palisades.
Chapel Court
A modest courtyard with a makeshift wooden shrine, where prayers are offered for protection and morale.
Ditch and Palisade
A defensive ditch dug before the palisade slows attackers and exposes them to missile fire. The wall is further heightened and strengthened.
Firing Platform
A simple raised wooden platform behind the walls, providing archers better sightlines and angles for defending the fort.
Granary Store
A rudimentary granary of raised wood platforms, providing safer and larger storage for harvested grains and dried foods.
Training Square
A patch of trampled earth and makeshift dummies where local levies drill with spear and shield. The beginnings of organized defense.
Spiked Ditch
A shallow ditch filled with sharpened stakes, designed to injure and slow attackers.
Lookout Post
A rough wooden platform atop earth mounds, manned by a handful of sentries with tents and a fire pit. Offers basic warning of approaching enemies.
Well House
A timber shack covers the newly dug well, providing vital water for the garrison and livestock. Defenders may now withstand longer sieges.
Reinforced Palisade
Sturdier wooden stakes, set deeper and bound together, form this wall. It offers improved defense and withstands basic assaults and fire.
Stable Yard
A simple, fenced enclosure where horses are tethered and basic feed is stored. Essential for rapid movement and scouting in rough territory.
Shallow Ditch
A simple defensive ditch dug by hand, offering rudimentary protection and slowing attackers.
Militia Hut
A rough shelter built from timber and turf, providing the most basic protection and gathering point for a handful of local defenders.
Arrow Slit Wall
A makeshift palisade reinforced with basic wooden arrow slits, allowing defenders to fire from relative safety. Represents the first steps in organized fortification on the frontier.
Tool Shed
A makeshift shelter built from logs and earth, serving as storage for basic tools and a workbench for simple repairs. Essential for the first steps of fortification.
Simple Gate
A basic wooden gate, hastily erected from logs and earth, serving as the first line of defense for new settlements.
Courtyard Clearing
A rough, hastily cleared patch of earth in the heart of the fort. Here, tents are pitched and basic supplies are stored, serving as the first mustering ground for defenders.
Food Shed
A makeshift shelter of timber and thatch for basic food storage, hastily built by settlers to keep supplies dry and safe from animals.
Wooden Fence
A hastily erected barrier of sharpened logs and brambles, marking the edge of settled territory and providing the most basic protection against wild beasts and opportunistic raiders.
